subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

The inspector __smile__ after he was finished and patted Margie’s head.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"smile"** means to form one's features into a pleased, kind, or amused expression, typically with the corners of the mouth turned up and the front teeth exposed. (मुस्कुराना)

 
 
• **Example: **She couldn't help but **smile** when she saw the surprise party.
 
 
 
• **"Smiled" **is the past tense of "smile", indicating that the action has already happened. (मुस्कुराया)
 
 
• **Example: **He **smiled **warmly at the guests as they entered the room.
 
 

Hence, the correct substitution for the given sentence is **'smiled'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **has smiled **(मुस्कुराया है): Indicates a present perfect tense, suggesting the action happened at an unspecified time before now.

 
 
• **Example:** She has smiled at everyone she met today.
 
 
 
• **was smiled** (मुस्कुराया गया): This is incorrect usage because "smile" is not typically used in the passive voice.
 
 
• **Example:** Incorrect: He was smiled by the crowd.
 
 
 
• **No substitution required** (कोई प्रतिस्थापन आवश्यक नहीं): This would be correct if the original sentence was accurate, but it is not in this case.

 

4e:Tc55,

The correct answer is: **Option 2.**
